# Vector index benchmark, 2026-11-19 15:52

pgvector HNSW against ParadeDB's native vector index, on the Kith catalog (25,000 products, text-embedding-3-small at 768 dims) and the 55 labelled queries in evals/ground_truth.jsonl.

- Servers: pdb026 = Postgres 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2), pg_search 0.26.1, pgvector 0.8.6; pdb027 = Postgres 18.7 (Debian 18.7-1.pgdg13+2), pg_search 0.27.0, pgvector 0.8.6. Docker, shared_buffers 512MB, same settings on both.
- Machine: macOS-27.2.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O, 12 CPUs (Docker Desktop's VM limits apply).
- Each search asks for 50 candidates (what hybrid search fuses); quality is scored @10.
- Latency: client-side, one connection, warm, 10 passes over every query; one SQL statement per search, session settings set beforehand.
- Query vectors are precomputed (evals/bench/query_vectors.jsonl): no OpenAI calls, identical input.

## Approximate vs exact nearest neighbours, and latency

Recall vs exact = share of the true nearest neighbours (brute-force search, same filters) the index returned. Latency is the vector query alone, over 55 queries x 10 passes, with each case's own filters.

## Which filters run inside the ParadeDB index

EXPLAIN of the ParadeDB vector search with each filter alone, written by the app's filters.build_where exactly as search writes it. Clause = what the filter added to the query ParadeDB runs: term / range / ... are lookups in the index; other kinds (a column not in the index, an expression like lower(brand)) are checked row by row during the scan.

| Filter | Plan | Clause kind | Clause added to the scan |
|---|---|---|---|
| is_active, in_stock (default) | pushed into the scan | - | - |
| sold out included | pushed into the scan | - | - |
| on_sale | pushed into the scan | term | `{"term":{"field":"on_sale","value":true}}` |
| price_min <= x (max price) | pushed into the scan | range | `{"range":{"field":"price_min","lower_bound":null,"upper_bound":{"included":"100"}}}` |
| price_max >= x (min price) | pushed into the scan | range | `{"range":{"field":"price_max","lower_bound":{"included":"100"},"upper_bound":null}}` |
| gender = ANY(...) | pushed into the scan | term_set | `{"term_set":{"terms":[{"field":"gender","value":"womens"},{"field":"gender","value":"unisex"}]}}` |
| NOT gender = ANY(...) (exclude) | pushed into the scan | boolean | `{"boolean":{"should":[{"boolean":{"must":["all"],"must_not":[{"exists":{"field":"gender"}}]}},{"boolean":{"must":[{"boolean":{"must":[{"exis…` |
| category = ANY(...) | pushed into the scan | term_set | `{"term_set":{"terms":[{"field":"category","value":"footwear"}]}}` |
| lower(brand) = ANY(...) OR collaborator | pushed into the scan | boolean | `{"boolean":{"should":[{"heap_filter":{"indexed_query":"all","always_filters":[{"heap_filter":"(lower(brand) = ANY ('{nike}'::text[]))"}]}},{…` |
| NOT lower(coalesce(brand)) ... (exclude) | pushed into the scan | heap_filter | `{"heap_filter":{"indexed_query":{"heap_filter":{"indexed_query":{"boolean":{"must":[{"with_index":{"query":{"all":{"field":"product_id"}}}},…` |
| sizes_available && ... (not indexed) | pushed into the scan | heap_filter | `{"heap_filter":{"indexed_query":{"boolean":{"must":[{"with_index":{"query":{"all":{"field":"product_id"}}}},{"term":{"field":"is_active","va…` |
| subcategory = ANY(...) | pushed into the scan | term_set | `{"term_set":{"terms":[{"field":"subcategory","value":"low top sneakers"}]}}` |

## Hybrid in one SQL statement (E)

BM25 (`|||`, pdb.score) and the vector search (`<=>`) as two CTEs over the same ParadeDB index, fused with RRF in SQL, against the app's way: the two searches on two connections at the same time, fused in Python. Plain RRF in both (weights 1, k = 60, 50 candidates per branch), same filters in both branches.

- Same top 10 from both: **55/55** queries.
- One statement: p50 8.72 ms, p95 10.26 ms; with parallel workers off (max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 0): p50 4.50 ms, p95 6.25 ms. Two queries in parallel + Python: p50 6.69 ms, p95 7.74 ms.
- nDCG@10: one statement 0.736; the app's hybrid on C 0.778 (its extra rules: style codes to BM25 alone, fuzzy retry, BM25 weight by query coverage).
- Vector branch in the index's Top K scan: yes.
